text:
Fixed, with an API change. calculate_effective_df() no longer applies the 1/(1 + 2*sum(1 - k/n)) factor - it had no basis, never depended on the fitted coefficients, and was applied on top of whitening. New contract: method='residual' (default, alias 'simple') returns n - p; method='satterthwaite' takes X and resid_cov and computes tr(RV)^2/tr(RVRV) via a new .satterthwaite_df() helper, which reduces exactly to n - p when V = I. AR order alone no longer reduces df, because fmrireg whitens before fitting; genuine shortfall from imperfect whitening is what Satterthwaite measures. Robust weights still scale multiplicatively by mean(w), and all-zero weights now correctly floor at 1.

Also fixed: method='satterthwaite' was previously a verbatim duplicate of 'simple'.

Testing (tests/testthat/test-effective-df-correctness.R, 46 assertions): exact reduction to n - p when V = I across several n and p; agreement with a brute-force explicit-R trace computation on four covariance regimes; scale invariance; strict monotonic decrease in df as autocorrelation rises; bounds 1 <= df <= n - p; rank-deficient design handled; robust and Satterthwaite adjustments compose multiplicatively; and two Monte Carlo calibration gates - null p-values uniform by KS with rejection rates within 1.2pp of alpha=.05 and 0.6pp of alpha=.01 over 4000 reps, plus Satterthwaite calibrating OLS t statistics under AR(1) errors. Regression guards assert the old 62.9 and 37.8 values cannot return.

Three existing tests asserted the buggy deflation (test_effective_df.R:16,20,30) and were rewritten to the correct contract; the change-detector in test-variance-closed-form.R has done its job and now asserts the fix. Full suite: 2679 pass / 0 fail / 0 error.
